title: Blind Spots
subject: psychology
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: Ten entries on the reliable ways a mind goes wrong.
completionMessage: You saw that coming, of course.

entries.clue: Amos who wrote with Kahneman on judgement under uncertainty
___ cost, gone but still steering the decision
One good trait lending its glow to the rest
Pull exerted by whatever number came first
Head start enjoyed by the first item on a list
Why the last thing said lingers longest
___'s fallacy, the belief that a coin owes you a tail
David whose name is hyphenated to Kruger's

factCards.text: Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman described anchoring, availability and representativeness in a 1974 paper in Science.
factCards.sourceTitle: Tversky and Kahneman, 'Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases', Science (1974)

factCards.text: Justin Kruger and David Dunning reported in 1999 that people who performed worst on a task tended to overestimate their performance most.
factCards.sourceTitle: Kruger and Dunning, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (1999)

factCards.text: Primacy and recency together give the serial position curve: items at the beginning and end of a list are recalled better than those in the middle.
